quizzes.title: India's Solar Position and Records
quizzes.passage:
India's solar sector is tracked in the IRENA Renewable Energy Statistics 2026. According to this report, India emerged as the world's second largest solar growth market in 2025, while China remained the largest. Global solar power capacity also rose sharply over the same year, showing how quickly the sector has expanded. India further moved up in power production, overtaking a major economy to become the world's third largest solar power producer in 2025. In total renewable energy installed capacity, India was placed third globally. The report also records India's installed solar capacity for 2025.

India's projects include several large and notable installations. Bhadla Solar Park in Rajasthan is among the major solar parks in the country. Omkareshwar in Madhya Pradesh is a floating solar plant, and it is India's largest of its kind. Rajarhat was India's first floating solar power plant. Naukh, India's first commercial solar thermal power plant, is developed by Godawari Green Energy. Indian Railways' first solar power plant is at Bina, Madhya Pradesh. Dharnai in Bihar is India's first solar village. Guwahati Railway Station is India's first fully solar-powered railway station. The top solar states include Rajasthan, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra. Within the Extra Shots section, the booklet lists further solar projects in India.

questions.q: According to the IRENA Renewable Energy Statistics 2026, what was India's installed solar capacity in 2025?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives India's installed solar capacity as 150.26 GW in 2025, while 37 GW was the capacity added in that year.

questions.q: What is the installed capacity of the Omkareshwar floating solar plant?
questions.explanation: Omkareshwar in Madhya Pradesh is rated at 600 MW, while 2245 MW belongs to Bhadla Solar Park.

questions.q: In which state is Modhera, India's first 24x7 solar-powered village?
questions.explanation: The booklet places Modhera, India's first 24x7 solar-powered village, in Gujarat.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India emerged as the world's second largest solar growth market in 2025.
Reason (R): Bhadla Solar Park is located in Rajasthan.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Both statements are true in the booklet, but the location of Bhadla does not explain India's growth ranking.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Bhadla Solar Park   ->   C. Khandwa
II. Omkareshwar   ->   D. Jaisalmer
III. Rajarhat   ->   B. Jodhpur
IV. Naukh   ->   A. Kolkata
questions.explanation: Bhadla Solar Park is in Jodhpur, Omkareshwar in Khandwa, Rajarhat in Kolkata and Naukh in Jaisalmer.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. China remained the largest solar market in 2025, adding 315 GW.
II. Global solar power capacity rose from 1880 GW in 2024 to 2392 GW in 2025.
III. Bhadla Solar Park has a capacity of 600 MW.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, whereas Bhadla Solar Park is rated at 2245 MW, not 600 MW.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Sanchi in Madhya Pradesh is India's first solar city.
II. Rajarhat was India's first floating solar power plant, set up in 2015.
III. Modhera in Gujarat is India's first solar village.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are in the booklet, while Dharnai in Bihar, not Modhera, is India's first solar village.

quizzes.title: Solar Records and Key Projects
quizzes.passage:
The IRENA Renewable Energy Statistics 2026 covers India's solar performance in 2025. In that year India became the world's second largest solar growth market, and China continued as the largest market. Global solar capacity rose sharply compared with the previous year. In solar power production, India moved up to third place in the world in 2025, after overtaking a major economy. The IRENA statistics also list India's installed solar capacity for 2025.

Several installations stand out in India. Omkareshwar in Madhya Pradesh is India's largest floating solar plant. Bhadla Solar Park is located in Rajasthan and is one of the country's major solar parks. Naukh, in Rajasthan, is India's first commercial solar thermal power plant, developed by Godawari Green Energy. Modhera in Gujarat is India's first 24x7 solar-powered village. Sanchi in Madhya Pradesh is recognised as India's first solar city. Rajarhat, in Kolkata, was India's first floating solar power plant. Guwahati Railway Station is India's first fully solar-powered railway station. The top solar states include Rajasthan, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra. Global solar capacity increased from one year to the next, as shown by the IRENA statistics. The booklet lists these projects under a section titled Extra Shots. Naukh and Bhadla are both located in Rajasthan.

questions.q: How many GW of solar capacity did India add in 2025, according to the IRENA Renewable Energy Statistics 2026? (in GW)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that India added 37 GW of solar capacity in 2025.

questions.q: Which country did India overtake to become the world's third largest solar power producer in 2025?
questions.explanation: The booklet says India overtook Japan to become the third largest solar power producer in 2025.

questions.q: What is the capacity of Bhadla Solar Park in Jodhpur? (in MW)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives Bhadla Solar Park, Jodhpur, Rajasthan, a capacity of 2245 MW.

questions.q: In which year was Rajarhat, India's first floating solar power plant, set up?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Rajarhat in Kolkata, India's first floating solar plant, was set up in 2015.

questions.q: Which Indian state has Dharnai village, recognised as India's first solar village?
questions.explanation: The booklet identifies Dharnai in Bihar as India's first solar village.

questions.q: What was global solar power capacity in 2025? (in GW)
questions.explanation: The booklet says global solar capacity rose from 1880 GW in 2024 to 2392 GW in 2025.

questions.q: Naukh, India's first commercial solar thermal power plant, is in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: The booklet places Naukh in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, and it is developed by Godawari Green Energy.

quizzes.title: Climate Commitments and Global Initiatives
quizzes.passage:
India's climate commitments are known collectively as Panchamrita. The package includes a net zero target, and the country aims to meet 50 percent of its energy requirements from renewable energy by 2030. India also aims to reduce its total projected carbon emissions by one billion tonnes from now till 2030. The commitments are presented as a single list in the booklet, separate from the collaborative efforts discussed below. Each target in the Panchamrita list is given a time frame in the booklet, either a specific year or the period up to 2030.

Under the heading of major collaborative initiatives, the booklet lists several efforts. The Global Solar Facility is listed first among them, and it is one initiative that supports solar investment. STAR-C stands for Solar Technology Application and Resource Centres, and it works on solar technologies. The OSOWOG concept seeks to integrate regional grids across Asia, the Middle East, Africa and Europe for 24-hour renewable power. India first proposed the concept at the Inaugural Assembly of the International Solar Alliance. The booklet names that assembly as the setting for the proposal, and it presents each initiative with a short description of its aim. Taken together, these entries form the booklet's list of major collaborative initiatives.

questions.q: Under Panchamrita, India's net zero target is to be achieved by which year?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that India aims to achieve net zero by the year 2070.

questions.q: At which COP summit was the Global Solar Facility launched?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Global Solar Facility was launched at COP27 in 2022.

questions.q: What is the target for non-fossil energy capacity under Panchamrita by 2030?
questions.explanation: The booklet sets the non-fossil energy capacity target at 500 GW by 2030.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Global Solar Facility was launched at COP26 in Glasgow.
Reason (R): The Global Solar Facility provides payment guarantees to de-risk solar investments.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The Global Solar Facility was launched at COP27, so A is false, while its provision of payment guarantees is correctly stated in R.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Global Solar Facility   ->   B. Training of engineers, entrepreneurs and policymakers
II. STAR-C   ->   D. India's climate commitments at COP26 in Glasgow
III. One Sun, One World, One Grid   ->   A. Payment guarantees to de-risk solar investments
IV. Panchamrita   ->   C. Trans-national solar power connectivity
questions.explanation: The Global Solar Facility gives payment guarantees, STAR-C trains engineers, One Sun One World One Grid advocates trans-national connectivity, and Panchamrita is India's climate commitments at COP26.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Global Solar Facility was launched at COP27.
II. India first proposed the OSOWOG concept during the ISA's Inaugural Assembly.
III. The net zero target under Panchamrita is 2050.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, whereas the Panchamrita net zero target is 2070, not 2050.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Panchamrita commitments were announced at COP26 in Glasgow.
II. The Global Solar Facility provides payment guarantees to de-risk solar investments.
III. STAR-C trains only engineers in solar technologies.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are in the booklet, while STAR-C trains engineers, entrepreneurs and policymakers, not only engineers.

quizzes.title: Panchamrita Targets and Solar Initiatives
quizzes.passage:
India's climate commitments, called Panchamrita, were announced at COP26 in Glasgow. The first of these commitments is to achieve net zero by the year 2070. Another is to increase non-fossil energy capacity to 500 GW by 2030, and a third is to meet a large share of energy needs from renewables. The booklet presents these commitments under a separate heading from the collaborative efforts that follow. Each target in the Panchamrita list is given a time frame in the booklet, either a specific year or the period up to 2030.

Several initiatives support solar energy. One initiative, launched at a major climate conference, offers payment guarantees to lower the risk of solar investments and help attract commercial financing. A programme of solar resource centres trains engineers, entrepreneurs and policymakers in solar technologies. A further concept advocates trans-national solar power connectivity, and it was presented at COP26 jointly with a partner country. The concept seeks to integrate regional grids across Asia, the Middle East, Africa and Europe for 24-hour renewable power. The booklet describes the initiatives in its own section, following the Panchamrita list, with their aims and functions. These efforts appear under the booklet's list of major collaborative initiatives, and each initiative has its own entry.

questions.q: What percentage of its energy requirements does India aim to meet from renewable energy by 2030? (in per cent)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the target of meeting 50 percent of energy requirements from renewable energy by 2030.

questions.q: By how many billion tonnes does India aim to reduce its total projected carbon emissions from now till 2030? (in billion tonnes)
questions.explanation: The booklet states the goal as a reduction of one billion tonnes of projected emissions from now till 2030.

questions.q: In which year was the Global Solar Facility launched?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Global Solar Facility was launched at COP27 in 2022.

questions.q: Which initiative provides payment guarantees to de-risk solar investments?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Global Solar Facility as providing payment guarantees to de-risk solar investments.

questions.q: Which initiative trains engineers, entrepreneurs and policymakers in solar technologies? (acronym)
accept: Solar Technology Application and Resource Centres
questions.explanation: The booklet describes STAR-C as the initiative that trains engineers, entrepreneurs and policymakers in solar energy technologies.

questions.q: Which concept advocates trans-national solar power connectivity? (acronym)
accept: One Sun, One World, One Grid
One Sun One World One Grid
questions.explanation: The booklet says One Sun, One World, One Grid, known as OSOWOG, advocates trans-national solar power connectivity.

questions.q: Along with India, which country co-advocated the One Sun, One World, One Grid concept at COP26? (name the country)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists One Sun, One World, One Grid as an India and UK initiative at COP26.
